people.name: Nikos Tsinopoulos
people.biography: Nikos Tsinopoulos served as president from 1975 to 1977, founding the artistic gymnastics department (April 1975), harmonising the constitution with Law 75/1975, and organising the celebrated 7th Dia Games in 1977.

people.name: Theodoros Diamantopoulos
people.biography:
Theodoros Diamantopoulos led Archelaos from 2011 to 2019, securing the handball team's return to the top flight (A1/Handball Premier) and successfully reviving the Dia Games in 2016. Under his presidency, on 20 November 2014 the club moved its offices into premises provided by the Municipality of Katerini at the 1st DAK (3A Ethnikou Stadiou Street), reducing substantial rent and shared-building costs (Board minutes no. 26, 20 November 2014).

The revived 'Dia en Olympo 2016' athletics meeting on 28 May 2016 brought together approximately 200 athletes from 30 clubs, according to the club's event archive.

people.name: Panagiotis Diamantopoulos
people.biography:
Panagiotis Diamantopoulos was unanimously elected president of Archelaos in September 2026, leading the club during its historic 70th anniversary celebrations (1956–2026).

He served as second vice-president and gymnastics director following the April 2025 board elections. In a September 2026 interview, he discussed plans to present a 70th-anniversary historical volume, a project initiated by his predecessor Alkinoos Tasopoulos.

people.name: Stavros Diamantopoulos
people.biography: Physical education teacher Stavros Diamantopoulos was the founder and first voluntary coach of Archelaos's artistic gymnastics department in April 1975, leading the team to its first national championship appearance.

people.name: Orestis Darlagiannis
people.biography: Physical education educator and an early official for volleyball and gymnastics at Archelaos, also associated with school sport and the DIÏA games.

people.name: Elisavet Pesiridou
people.biography: Elisavet Pesiridou, developed in Archelaos's athletics academy, won the 2013 Greek indoor 60 m hurdles title (8.56) and went on to represent Greece at two Olympic Games (Rio 2016, Tokyo 2021).

people.name: Kostas Koukodimos
people.biography: Long jumper Kostas Koukodimos represented Archelaos under coaches Takis Paraskevopoulos and Giannis Papargyriou. He placed sixth at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, won Mediterranean gold in 1991 and European Indoor silver in Paris on 13 March 1994 with 8.09 m. He recorded 8.36 m at the Venizelia meeting in Chania on 5 June 1994, a Greek outdoor record. The 8.09 m Paris result belongs to Koukodimos, not Konstantinos Vasileiadis.

people.name: Antonis Papadimitriou
people.biography: Antonis Papadimitriou was Greece's premier javelin thrower, setting world junior marks, winning the 1984 Balkan title, and holding the Greek national record of 79.56 m.

people.name: Athina Papasotiriou
people.biography: Athina Papasotiriou set the Greek indoor pentathlon record (4,251 pts, 1996), scored 5,758 pts in the heptathlon at the European Cup in Riga, and won national titles in long jump (1991) and heptathlon (1994, 1996).

people.name: Katerina Dalaka
people.biography: Katerina Dalaka developed through Archelaos's track academy, setting Greek youth and scholastic records in the 300 m and 400 m hurdles.

people.name: Kyriakos Saralis
people.biography: Kyriakos Saralis served as treasurer of Archelaos in 1975, managing the club's finances during its constitutional reform and the expansion into artistic gymnastics.

people.name: Efstathios Z. Zannas
people.biography: Physical education teacher Efstathios Zannas founded Archelaos handball (1976), organised swimming (1980), established the historic 15.5 km "Dios Dromos" road race (1987), and served as club president (1985–1989).

people.name: Alkinoos Tasopoulos
people.biography:
Alkis Tasopoulos set a club record of 9:42.2 in the 3,000 m steeplechase in 1971 and served as president from 2019 until his death in July 2026, leading the club's modern reorganisation and facility modernisation.

In September 2025, as serving president, he attended the municipality's formal reception for world U17 wrestling silver medallist Dimitris Soulis.

people.name: Lazaros Psomiadis
people.biography: Lazaros Psomiadis proposed the establishment of Archelaos wrestling in April 1978 and became its first head coach on 1 January 1980, laying the foundation for world and European wrestling medals.

people.name: Nikolaos Zamanis
people.biography: Greek-Roman wrestler Nikolaos Zamanis, son of wrestling department official Michalis Zamanis, earned world junior silver in Israel (1990, 81 kg), Mediterranean gold (1993, 82 kg), and a European bronze in 1988. He won Greek senior titles in 1993 and 1994 and served as wrestling coach from October 1997 to April 1999.

people.name: Alexios Poulikidis
people.biography: Alexios Poulikidis won heavyweight bronze (115 kg) at the 1988 European Junior Championships in Izmir and placed 6th in West Germany in 1989, dominating domestic heavyweight wrestling.

people.name: Savvas Tsentidis
people.biography: Former heavyweight Greco-Roman wrestler and long-standing Archelaos coach. He led youth wrestling success and coached Dimitris Soulis to World U17 silver in 2025.

people.name: Kostas Tamos
people.biography:
Wrestling coach Kostas Tamos is part of the coaching team behind Archelaos's recent national titles and international podium finishes, including the 2025 World U17 silver.

The Municipality of Katerini named him among the coaches behind Dimitris Soulis's 2025 world U17 wrestling silver medal.

people.name: Kostas Zinisa
people.biography:
Wrestling coach Kostas Zinisa contributes to Archelaos's wrestling academy, preparing the successful junior squads that secured national championships in 2024 and 2025.

Municipal announcements identify him as a wrestling coach at Archelaos in 2024 and again in connection with Dimitris Soulis's 2025 world U17 silver medal.

people.name: Kyriakos Konstantinidis
people.biography:
Kyriakos Konstantinidis, wrestling department director, provided the organisational leadership behind Archelaos's 2025 national U20 team championship and international medals.

The Municipality of Katerini expressly acknowledged his contribution as wrestling department director following Dimitris Soulis's world U17 silver medal in July 2025.

people.name: Ioannis Petkos
people.biography: Ioannis Petkos developed through Archelaos's wrestling academy, winning 1st place and the gold medal at the Greek National Cadet Wrestling Championships. He was officially honoured during the department's 40th anniversary celebrations in May 2019.

people.name: Elevtherios Charitidis
people.biography: Eleftherios Charitidis earned national gold medals in both the Schoolboys (Pampaides) and Cadet (Paides) divisions, representing Archelaos with distinction across multiple youth age groups.

people.name: Sokratis Konstantinidis
people.biography: Sokratis Konstantinidis won national Schoolboys gold in 2019 and captured a bronze medal at the 2025 Greek National U20 Championships in Serres, helping Archelaos claim the overall team championship.

people.name: Georgios Athanasiou
people.biography: Georgios Athanasiou secured 1st place and the gold medal at the Greek National Schoolboys Wrestling Championships, receiving honors at the club's 40th anniversary gala in 2019.

people.name: Georgios Athanasiou
people.role: Administration · Board member and athletics department official
people.biography: Member of the current Board of Directors of G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis and official responsible for the athletics (track and field) department. He is a different person from the wrestler of the same name also listed in the Hall of Fame.

people.name: Maria Mitsiopoulou
people.biography: Maria Mitsiopoulou won the Greek National Junior Women's Wrestling Championship, carrying forward Archelaos's pioneering tradition in women's wrestling that dates back to 1986.

people.name: Dimitrios Mitsiopoulos
people.biography: Dimitrios Mitsiopoulos achieved 2nd place and the silver medal at the Greek National Cadet Wrestling Championships, contributing significantly to Archelaos's national team points.

people.name: Freideriki Paniori
people.biography: Freideriki Paniori captured the bronze medal at the Greek National Cadet Girls' Wrestling Championships, honoured in 2019 as a prominent member of Archelaos's female wrestling squad.

people.name: Christina Voulgari
people.biography: Christina Voulgari earned the national bronze medal at the Greek Cadet Girls' Wrestling Championships, celebrated at the club's 2019 historical anniversary.

people.name: Theocharis Anastasiadis
people.biography: Theocharis Anastasiadis won bronze at the Greek National Cadet Wrestling Championships, recognised among the distinguished young athletes of Archelaos in 2019.

people.name: Georgios Michailidis
people.biography: Georgios Michailidis placed 3rd, winning the bronze medal at the Greek National Schoolboys Wrestling Championships, demonstrating the strength of the club's youth academy.

people.name: Levteris Pappas
people.biography: Lefteris Pappas won the gold medal at the 2025 Greek National U20 Greco-Roman Wrestling Championships in Serres, propelling Archelaos to 1st place in the team standings with 79 points.

people.name: Dimitris Pappas
people.biography: Dimitris Pappas captured national gold at the 2025 Greek U20 Greco-Roman Championships in Serres, securing Archelaos's triumph as the top wrestling club in Greece.

people.name: Thanasis Evthymiadis
people.biography: Thanasis Efthymiadis took the silver medal at the 2025 Greek National U20 Wrestling Championships in Serres, reaching the finals and adding vital points to the club's team title.

people.name: Menelaos Voulgaris
people.biography: Menelaos Voulgaris claimed the bronze medal at the 2025 Greek National U20 Championships in Serres, contributing to the squad's six-medal haul that clinched the national club championship.

people.name: Nikos Mavridis
people.biography: Nikos Mavridis won bronze at the 2025 Greek U20 Wrestling Championships in Serres, completing Archelaos's six-medal sweep that secured the team championship with 79 points.

people.name: Theodoros Sfikas
people.biography:
Theodoros Sfikas, physical education teacher and 1973 board member, was the first coach and director of Archelaos basketball (1973–77) and the first volleyball coach (1973–76).

At Archelaos's 2022 anniversary event, he was honoured for his longstanding contribution to the basketball department.

people.name: Stamatia Kyparissi
people.biography:
Stamatia Kyparissi developed at Archelaos before becoming a standout wing spiker for the Greek Women's National Volleyball Team, representing the club's volleyball excellence.

In 2022, the club's anniversary commemoration recognised her as a leading historical representative of Archelaos volleyball.

people.name: Christos Lympanovnos
people.biography:
Former international gymnast Christos Lympanovnos took charge of Archelaos's boys' gymnastics in 2021, coaching Angelos Parousis to international Horizon Cup gold and national medals.

The club's 2022 commemorative celebration honoured him as a prominent representative of its artistic gymnastics history.

people.name: Savvas Karypidis
people.biography:
Savvas Karypidis, raised in Archelaos's academy, finished 6th at the 2004 Athens Olympics, was top scorer in the German Bundesliga (2008–09), and returned to lead Archelaos back to A1 in 2013.

At the 2022 club anniversary celebration, he was honoured as a leading representative of Archelaos handball.

people.name: Maria Faka
people.biography:
Maria Faka represented Greece at the 2004 Athens Olympics in air rifle, held the Greek national record of 395/400, won multiple national championships, and served as Archelaos head shooting coach.

She was honoured in the club's 2022 anniversary event as an outstanding representative of its shooting department.

people.name: Evangelia Saltsidou
people.biography:
Evangelia Saltsidou represented Archelaos in national and regional swimming championships, officially honoured at the club's 2022 historical gala as a leading figure in its swimming heritage.

Her recognition as a prominent representative of Archelaos swimming is documented in the list of honourees from the club's 2022 anniversary event.

people.name: Evangelos Charisis
people.biography:
Evangelos Charisis won the 2025 individual Greek recurve title, two team titles (2025, 2026), holds the national mixed U21 record, and ranked 9th in the world junior rankings.

In a 23 June 2026 announcement, the Municipality of Katerini confirmed his individual bronze medal at the national archery championships in Florina and Archelaos's first place in the overall standings.

people.name: Charis Iakovidis
people.biography:
Charis Iakovidis won back-to-back Greek recurve team championships with Archelaos (2025, 2026) and claimed consecutive individual national silver medals.

The Municipality of Katerini officially recorded his individual silver medal at the 2026 Greek National Archery Championships in Florina.

people.name: Vangelis Marinopoulos
people.biography:
Vangelis Marinopoulos won consecutive Greek recurve team titles with Archelaos (2025, 2026) and finished 5th individually at the 2026 national championships.

The Municipality of Katerini's 23 June 2026 announcement reports his fifth-place individual finish at the national archery championships in Florina.

people.name: Ioannis (Giannis) Charisis
people.role: Artistic Gymnastics · Athlete & Archery · Head Coach
people.biography: Ioannis (Giannis) Charisis competed in artistic gymnastics for Archelaos under coach Apostolos Samalis. The club’s men’s team won national team titles through the 1981–1991 era and again in 1993. Its documented 1991 and 1993 lineups included Charilaos Kakalis, Konstantinos Zaras, Evangelos Chrysopoulos, Ioannis Charisis and Alexandros Katsikakis. At the Greek Men’s Championships in Glyfada in 1991, Charisis placed third on parallel bars (7.600 points) and fourth on rings. Emmanouil Zaras served as a gymnastics department official, not as a competing member of the team. Charisis later became head coach of Archelaos archery, leading men’s Olympic recurve team championship wins in 2025 and 2026, Greek Cup wins in 2024 and 2026, and a first-place overall club ranking.

people.name: Dimitrios Galanis
people.biography:
Dimitrios Galanis, archery director and 2nd Vice President (2026), provided the administrative leadership behind Archelaos's 2025 and 2026 national archery championships.

The municipality acknowledged his role as archery director during the club's national triumph in June 2026; the published September 2026 board lists him as second vice-president and archery department director.

people.name: Konstantinos Myrotis
people.biography:
Konstantinos Myrotis organised Archelaos shooting (1983) and officially founded the archery department in late 1993, pioneering target sports in Katerini.

The club's Greek Wikipedia entry credits him with an initiative leading to the creation of its archery department, which began operating in late 1993.

people.name: Anargyros Kapetanakis
people.biography:
Anargyros Kapetanakis served as shooting official (1983), swimming director (1984), and co-founded the archery department in 1993 alongside Konstantinos Myrotis.

The Greek-language club entry names him as a department director involved in establishing Archelaos archery in late 1993.

Additional historical notes record his service as shooting section director also in 1993–1994, alongside his wider administrative contribution during 1983–1995.

people.name: Dionysis Evthymiadis
people.biography: Dionysis Efthymiadis was appointed the first official director of Archelaos's wrestling section on 16 September 1980, establishing the foundational administrative and training structures of the sport.

people.name: Dimitris Giannaros
people.biography: Dimitrios Giannaros presided over Archelaos (1977–1985) during its greatest expansion, establishing handball, wrestling, swimming, shooting, water polo, and weightlifting, before his untimely death in office in July 1985.

people.name: Miltiadis Mavroeidis
people.biography: Head swimming coach Miltiadis Mavroeidis directed Archelaos's competitive swimming team to multiple national podium finishes (including two silvers and one bronze) at the 2025 Greek Championships.

people.name: Georgios Diamantidis
people.biography: Swimming coach Georgios Diamantidis plays a vital role in youth development and technical training, preparing Archelaos swimmers for top-tier national championship competition.

people.name: Georgios Evthymiou
people.biography: Physical Education Inspector Georgios Efthymiou (1908–2006) founded Archelaos on 29 April 1956, authored its first constitution, secured its legal recognition, and served as its inaugural president, establishing track and field throughout Pieria.

people.name: Athanasios Tsaknakis
people.biography: Athanasios Tsaknakis was active during Archelaos Katerinis’ formative years. According to a summary of the club’s 40th-anniversary commemorative book (pp. 11–13), he headed its first elected board following legal recognition in 1957, working alongside vice-president Ioannis Zarogiannis and treasurer Theodoros Xiromeritis to establish its administration and support early athletics activities. The distinction between the founding leadership and the first elected board remains subject to checking the original records.

people.name: Theofilos Kamperidis
people.biography: Theofilos Kamperidis served as Archelaos president (1959–1961) and later as Mayor of Katerini and Member of Parliament, formally welcoming the 1990 Greek Cup-winning handball squad to the town square.

people.name: Takis Paraskevopoulos
people.biography: Takis Paraskevopoulos served as head track and field coach for 32 consecutive years (1964–1996), mentoring Greek champions, Balkan winners, and Olympians. The archival summary also records the 1973 recruitment of 20 pupils and the 1992 European school silver medal for Katerini’s 4th Lyceum.

people.name: Ioannis Ziogas
people.biography: Ioannis Ziogas was appointed the first head coach of Archelaos handball on 9 March 1978 and organized the first Northern Greece handball tournament in May 1978, launching the club's storied handball legacy. An additional archive summary refers to early organisation in February 1978; the 9 March 1978 minutes document his appointment.

people.name: Zaira Lazaridou
people.biography: Zaira Lazaridou set a Greek junior discus record of 43.80 m in May 1978 and later served as Archelaos track and field coach from 1985 to 1990.

people.name: Sokratis Skoufas
people.biography: Sokratis Skoufas was Archelaos's first international handball player (1981), coached the club to its 2nd Greek Cup triumph in 1994, beat RK Umag in Europe (1993), and returned to lead the 2013 A1 promotion.

people.name: Vasiliki Lazaridou
people.biography: Vasiliki Lazaridou has served as permanent secretary since 1983, embodying the administrative continuity and institutional memory of Archelaos across more than four decades.

people.name: Konstantinos Papadopoulos
people.biography: Konstantinos Papadopoulos served as the first swimming director (1981–1985). Following his death in 1985, Archelaos established the annual "Papadopouleia" swimming meet in his honour.

people.name: Dimitrios Papadimitriou
people.biography: Dimitrios Papadimitriou served as president from 1989 to 1993, overseeing the club's 1st Greek Handball Cup victory in 1990, its European debut, and the hosting of the 13th Balkan Youth Handball Championships in 1991.

people.name: Dimitris Soulis
people.role: Greco-Roman wrestling · U17 world silver medalist
people.biography:
Dimitris Soulis captured the world silver medal in the 71 kg Greco-Roman category at the 2025 U17 World Wrestling Championships in Athens, defeating Iran 9–8 in the semifinal.

ERT reported that he faced Uzbekistan's Behruzbek Valiev in the 2025 U17 world final, losing 3–1. In September 2025, he was officially welcomed and honoured by the Municipality of Katerini.

people.name: Christos Elevtheroudis
people.biography: Christos Eleftheroudis served as Archelaos president for 18 consecutive years (1993–2011), guiding the club to its 2nd Greek Handball Cup (1994), European competition, and founding the archery department (1993).

people.name: Elevtherios Stagkidis
people.biography: Eleftherios Stagkidis served as 1st Vice President in 2022 and track and field director, representing Archelaos in municipal consultations to upgrade stadium facilities at A' DAK.

people.name: Charalampos Savvidis
people.biography:
Charalampos Savvidis serves as 1st Vice President and handball director (2026), steering the administration of the men's national division team and academy operations at B' DAK.

The published September 2026 board lists him as first vice-president and handball department director.

people.name: Athanasios Mavroeidis
people.role: Administration · General Secretary and swimming official
people.biography: Elected General Secretary and long-standing swimming official, involved in federation relations and development of the club’s swimming teams.

people.name: Ioannis Samakovlis
people.biography: Ioannis Samakovlis served as club treasurer and archery director in 2022, managing finances and supporting the development of the outdoor archery range in Nea Chrani.

people.name: Michalis Kantartzis
people.biography: Michalis Kantartzis led press and public relations while serving as handball director in 2022, significantly boosting the club's media presence and community engagement.

people.name: Theodoros Seitanidis
people.biography: Theodoros Seitanidis served as shooting department director (2022–2024), maintaining shooting ranges at EAK and Neokaisareia and supporting national-level target shooters.

people.name: Vasileios Tzotzos
people.biography: Vasileios Tzotzos was appointed gymnastics director in 2022, facilitating the reorganisation of youth programmes and strengthening cooperation between coaching staff and the board.

people.name: Christos Tsimopoulos
people.biography: Christos Tsimopoulos served as volleyball director (2022–2024), representing the club in municipal facility negotiations and supporting competitive volleyball operations.

people.name: Pavlos Symeonidis
people.biography: Pavlos Symeonidis serves as treasurer and volleyball director (2026), overseeing financial administration and leading the development of men's and women's volleyball squads.

people.name: Angelos Parousis
people.biography: Angelos Parousis won international gold on floor and still rings, plus two silvers and two bronzes at the 2022 Horizon Cup, followed by three bronze medals at the 2023 Greek National Cadet Championships.

people.name: Fotios Parthenidis
people.biography: Fotios Parthenidis joined Archelaos's coaching staff in October 1991, mentoring gymnasts across three decades and coaching the girls' squad to regional bronze (2024) and 4th nationally (2023).

people.name: Vasileios Kalpakidis
people.biography: Former club champion Vasileios Kalpakidis took over as gymnastics coach in 2021, guiding the cadet girls to regional all-around bronze in 2024 and national championship finals.

people.name: Fani Gkiousooglou
people.biography: Fani Giousooglou serves as coach and choreographer for Archelaos gymnastics, orchestrating the routines that secured national podium finishes and regional floor gold in 2024.

people.name: Nikoleta Tsaroucha
people.biography: Nikoleta Tsaroucha won regional gold on floor exercise and bronze in the team all-around at Mikra in March 2024, placing 6th nationally in the team all-around with Archelaos.

people.name: Kalliopi Georganta
people.biography: Kalliopi Georganta won balance beam bronze and team all-around bronze at Mikra in 2024, after finishing 4th in the team all-around at the 2023 National Championships in Lavrio.

people.name: Theodora Amexizidou
people.biography: Theodora Amexizidou was an integral member of the Archelaos gymnastics team that claimed regional all-around bronze in 2024 and competed at consecutive national championships.

people.name: Lampriani Sotiriou
people.biography: Lambriani Sotiriou achieved exceptional results at the 2024 Greek National Championships: 4th all-around, 4th floor, 4th vault, 6th beam, and 8th uneven bars.

people.name: Ermioni Valvi
people.biography: Ermioni Valvi was a key performer in Archelaos's squad that finished 4th in the team all-around at the 2023 National Championships and 6th in 2024.

people.name: Sofia Nikolaidou
people.biography: Sofia Nikolaidou reached the individual apparatus finals at the 2024 Greek National Championships, finishing 8th on floor exercise and 6th in the team all-around.

people.name: Athanasios Dimopoulos
people.biography: Athanasios Dimopoulos captured the national bronze medal in Men's U21 Recurve Team competition at Loutraki in March 2023 alongside Evangelos Charisis and Nikolaos Ntamposis.

people.name: Nikolaos Ntamposis
people.biography: Nikolaos Ntamposis captured the national bronze medal in the Men's U21 Recurve Team event at the Greek National Championships in Loutraki (March 2023), alongside Evangelos Charisis and Athanasios Dimopoulos, marking a significant milestone for Archelaos's youth archery programme.

people.name: Giorgos Karadimos
people.biography:
Giorgos Karadimos scored in both Greek Cup finals (1990, 1994) and co-coached Archelaos back to the A1 division in 2013.

As a player, he scored in both of Archelaos’ victorious Greek Cup finals, in 1990 and 1994.

people.name: Tasos Papadopoulos
people.biography: Tasos Papadopoulos served as primary goalkeeper for Archelaos's men's handball team during its return to the top flight (A1 Division and Handball Premier) from 2013 to 2016 under head coaches Sokratis Skoufas and Giorgos Karadimos.

people.name: Fotis Tziokas
people.biography:
Fotis Tziokas played as pivot for Archelaos men's handball team between 2013 and 2016, providing physical strength, interior scoring, and defensive grit during the club's campaigns in the A1 Division and Handball Premier.

Additional archival note: Listed in the club’s mini or boys’ handball squads during the 1990s.

people.name: Charis Terzopoulos
people.biography: Charis Terzopoulos featured as a pivot in Archelaos's handball roster during its top-division resurgence (2013–2016), contributing on both ends of the court in the Greek A1 and Handball Premier leagues.

people.name: Giorgos Xefteris
people.biography: Giorgos Xefteris played as pivot and central defender for Archelaos from 2013 to 2016, providing critical defensive stability during the club's top-tier Handball Premier presence.

people.name: Apostolos Englezos
people.biography: Apostolos Englezos developed through Archelaos's youth ranks and competed as a pivot for the senior team in Greece's premier handball leagues from 2013 to 2016.

people.name: Panagiotis Samlidis
people.biography:
Panagiotis Samlidis was the primary playmaker and on-court leader for Archelaos handball during its 2013–2016 top-flight tenure, renowned for his court vision, tactical execution, and clutch scoring.

Additional archival note: Listed in the club’s mini or boys’ handball squads during the 1990s.

people.name: Nikos Drantzios
people.biography: Nikos Drantzios was a dynamic left wing for Archelaos (2013–2016), known for his fast-break execution, sharp corner shooting, and defensive intensity in the Greek top division.

people.name: Vangelis Raptis
people.biography:
Α1 και στη Handball Premier (2013–2016). Vangelis Raptis played as right wing for Archelaos from 2013 to 2016, providing scoring efficiency on counterattacks and reliable perimeter shooting in the national top flight.

Additional archival note: Listed in the club’s mini or boys’ handball squads during the 1990s.

people.name: Spyros Triantafyllou
people.biography: Spyros Triantafyllou served as playmaker and backcourt player for Archelaos during its top-division run (2013–2016), bolstering the team's ball distribution and offensive depth.

people.name: Nikos Voutsas
people.biography: Nikos Voutsas was a backcourt shooter for Archelaos (2013–2016), contributing long-range firepower and defensive physicality in Greece's premier handball division.

people.name: Vasilis Kosmidis
people.biography: Vasilis Kosmidis was a goalkeeper on Archelaos's historic 1994 Greek Cup-winning team and returned two decades later (2013–2016) to anchor the defense in the A1 Division, personifying the club's enduring greatness.

people.name: Thanasis Xonis
people.biography: Thanasis Xonis competed as left wing for Archelaos (2013–2016), bringing speed, fast-break finishing, and perimeter defense to the top-flight squad.

people.name: Kostas Charalampidis
people.biography: Kostas Charalampidis directed play from the centre back/playmaker position for Archelaos (2013–2016), ensuring tactical discipline and ball flow against top national opposition.

people.name: Iraklis Kosmidis
people.biography: Iraklis Kosmidis served as goalkeeper for Archelaos's top-division handball team (2013–2016), providing solid goalkeeping depth in elite national competition.

people.name: Giorgos Asaridis
people.biography: Giorgos Asaridis anchored the pivot position for Archelaos (2013–2016), known for his physical defending, blocking, and positioning on the six-metre line.

people.name: Gavriil Saides
people.biography: Gavriil Saides played as left wing for Archelaos (2013–2016), delivering agile transitions, tight-angle finishes, and energetic wing play in Greece's highest league.

people.name: Stavros Konstantinidis
people.biography: Stavros Konstantinidis contributed as goalkeeper for Archelaos handball (2013–2016), playing a reliable role in the squad's top-tier campaigns.

people.name: Damir Desnica
people.biography: Serbian international Damir Desnica brought European experience and backcourt creativity to Archelaos (2013–2016), serving as an influential playmaker in the Handball Premier.

people.name: Giorgos Chrysos
people.biography: Giorgos Chrysos was a versatile backcourt player for Archelaos (2013–2016), contributing physical defense and penetrating attack in the Greek top division.

people.name: Periklis Chatzigiannis
people.biography:
Journalist Periklis Chatzigiannis researched, authored, and hosted the landmark 2022 Archelaos historical celebration at Ekavi Conference Centre, preserving the club's heritage through dedicated reporting.

On 22 September 2026, he published an interview with incoming president Panagiotis Diamantopoulos in Pieria News, discussing leadership continuity and a proposed 70th-anniversary commemorative volume.

people.name: Dimitrios Gatsios-Peseridis
people.biography: Dimitrios Gatsios-Peseridis directed the digital restoration and visual curation of Archelaos's photo and video archives for the 2022 historical retrospective at Ekavi Centre.

people.name: Dimitrios Adamopoulos
people.biography: Dimitrios Adamopoulos coordinated the overall logistics and event management for the 2022 Archelaos anniversary gala, bringing together generations of champions and club leaders.

people.name: Katerina Reha
people.biography: Katerina Reha won bronze at the 2025 Greek Outdoor Championships in the 100 m hurdles (13.93) and silver at the 2025 National Indoor Championships in the 60 m hurdles (8.42).

people.name: Nikos Zinisa
people.biography:
Nikos Zinisa achieved European glory by winning gold at the 2025 European U15 Wrestling Championships in Italy, followed by a gold medal at the 2026 Balkan Greco-Roman Championships representing Archelaos and Greece.

At the April 2025 Greek U17 wrestling championships in Larissa, he was listed among Archelaos's gold medallists as the club finished second in the boys' team standings.

His 2025 national U17 gold medal is explicitly recorded in coverage of Archelaos's second-place finish in the boys' team rankings.

people.name: Dimitris Charitidis

His bronze medal at the April 2025 national U17 championship in Larissa is confirmed in coverage of the team's results.

people.name: Michalis (Lakis) Charikleias
people.role: Men’s Handball Team Officer · Club Administrator
people.biography: Michalis (Lakis) Charikleias served as an officer of Archelaos’s men’s handball team and a member of the club administration during its demanding A1 National Division years. In his report for the 1998–99 season, coach Lefteris Eleftheriadis singled out the efforts of the team’s “sole officer” in securing financial support and resolving day-to-day problems. Charikleias also supported a structured medical-monitoring and injury-recording programme developed in collaboration with team physician Emmanouil Papakostas, coach Eleftheriadis and fitness coach K. Papadopoulos in 1998–99. The team physician specifically acknowledged his contribution to making the programme possible. In a 1999 memorandum, after more than ten years of service to sport, he represented the club’s position before sporting authorities. His legacy is one of sustained organisational support behind the scenes of Archelaos handball.

people.biography: Popi Charikleia-Athanasiadou was closely involved in the development of Archelaos handball, particularly the women’s team and youth programme. At the club elections of 11 March 1995, during Christos Eleftheroudis’s presidency, she was elected Second Vice-President of the Board of Directors. She served as an officer for the women’s handball team and the younger boys’, junior boys’ and junior girls’ squads. Club board minutes record her updates on youth results, including an eight-match unbeaten run by the younger boys’ team and a Fair Play Cup awarded to the junior boys. She is also mentioned as P. Charikleia-Athanasiadou among the officers associated with the development club GAS Orfeas (1991). Her work combined board responsibility, youth-team organisation and a continuing commitment to young athletes.

people.name: Vasilis (Vasileios) Efkarpidis
people.role: Board Member · Handball and Volleyball Officer · Supporter
people.biography: Vasilis (Vasileios) Efkarpidis served GAS Archelaos Katerinis for many years as a board member, sports-department officer and financial supporter. At the elections of 25 February 1989 he received the most votes, convened the meeting to constitute the new board and nominated Efstathios Zannas for president. In another election he ranked third with 76 votes; he was again involved in the club's administration in 2005–09. In March 1991 he became a handball officer, sharing responsibility for the men's and women's teams with Dimitrios Skamagas. During 1991–92 he assisted with the registration and integration of athletes from Northern Epirus. On 11 March 1992 he was formally assigned responsibility for the club's finances. As volleyball officer in 2005–07, he personally covered overnight accommodation costs for men's and women's away teams pending the release of grants. His company, 'EFKARPIDIS SA CINEMATOGRAPHIC ENTERPRISES', supported the club financially, including three separately recorded donations to volleyball: €2,000 in 2004, €1,800 in 2005, and €1,400 in 2007 (a total of €5,200), pending verification against the original minutes. people.name: Grigorios (Grigoris) Zannas
people.role: Track and Field Athlete · Sports Officer · General Secretary
people.biography:
Grigorios (Grigoris) Zannas, a pharmacist by profession, was associated with G.A.S. Archelaos Katerinis from as early as 1966, when he competed in track and field. He later moved from sport into administration, serving as an elected board member and assuming responsibility for several of the club’s sporting departments.

In 1990–91 he jointly oversaw athletics with Theodoros Diamantopoulos. In April 1991 he was also appointed joint officer for weightlifting as efforts were made to reactivate that department. He subsequently served as volleyball officer in 1991–92 and again in 1995–96. Board records from 1996 mention his resignation from the volleyball officer position and the board; it was initially not accepted by club president Christos Eleftheroudis.

His administrative service also included the post of General Secretary in 1999, as reflected in official club correspondence with sporting federations. His career, spanning athletics, several team departments and board administration, represents a long-standing contribution to Archelaos across different eras.
